AL.name: Alabama

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: Three times compensatory damages or $500,000, whichever is greater

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: No specific cap on medical malpractice damages

AL.notes: Alabama follows contributory negligence rule (complete bar to recovery)

AK.name: Alaska

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: No cap on general non-economic damages

AK.notes: Alaska has no damage caps for personal injury cases

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.notes: Arizona Constitution prohibits damage caps (Article 2, Section 31)

AR.name: Arkansas

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 or three times compensatory damages, whichever is less

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: Punitive damages in med mal limited to $250,000

AR.notes: Arkansas requires clear and convincing evidence for punitive damages

CA.name: California

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases (MICRA)

CA.notes: Prop 46 (2014) attempted to raise med mal cap but failed

CO.name: Colorado

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $642,430 cap on non-economic damages (adjusted for inflation annually)

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: $1,000,000 total cap on medical malpractice damages

wrongfulDeathCap.notes: No specific wrongful death cap beyond general non-economic cap

CO.notes: Colorado has strict caps on non-economic damages

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.notes: Connecticut has no statutory caps on damages

FL.name: Florida

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: Florida Supreme Court struck down med mal damage caps in 2017 (North Broward Hospital District v. Kalitan)

FL.notes: Florida previously had med mal caps that were ruled unconstitutional

GA.name: Georgia

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 cap on punitive damages unless specific intent to harm proven

GA.notes: Georgia previously had $350,000 non-economic cap ruled unconstitutional in 2010

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.notes: Hawaii does not allow punitive damages in most cases

ID.name: Idaho
ID.notes: Idaho has strict non-economic damage cap

IL.name: Illinois
IL.notes: Illinois Supreme Court ruled damage caps unconstitutional in 2010 (Lebron v. Gottlieb Memorial Hospital)

IN.name: Indiana

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $50,000 or three times compensatory damages, whichever is greater

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: $1,875,000 cap on total damages in medical malpractice cases (adjusted annually)

IN.notes: Indiana has one of the highest med mal caps

KS.name: Kansas
KS.notes: Kansas non-economic cap challenged but upheld

LA.name: Louisiana

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: No cap on damages but public hospitals have immunity limits

LA.notes: Louisiana does not allow punitive damages except in specific statutory cases

MD.name: Maryland

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $920,000 cap on non-economic damages (adjusted annually for inflation)
nonEconomicDamagesCap.wrongfulDeathRule: $2,300,000 cap on non-economic damages in wrongful death cases

wrongfulDeathCap.notes: Higher cap applies to wrongful death with multiple beneficiaries

MD.notes: Maryland has statutory caps on non-economic damages

MA.name: Massachusetts

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: No cap on damages; $500,000 cap on charitable immunity

MA.notes: Massachusetts has no general damage caps

MI.name: Michigan
MI.notes: Michigan previously had med mal caps that were ruled unconstitutional

MO.name: Missouri
MO.notes: Missouri Supreme Court struck down damage caps in 2012 (Watts v. Lester E. Cox Medical Centers)

NE.name: Nebraska

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: $2,750,000 cap on total damages in medical malpractice cases

NE.notes: Nebraska has one of the highest med mal caps

NV.name: Nevada

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $350,000 cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $300,000 if compensatory damages under $100,000; three times compensatory if over $100,000

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: Caps apply to med mal non-economic damages

NV.notes: Nevada has caps on med mal and punitive damages

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.notes: New Hampshire has no damage caps

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.notes: New Jersey has no damage caps

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.notes: New Mexico has no damage caps on private defendants

NY.name: New York
NY.notes: New York has no damage caps

NC.name: North Carolina

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $642,337 cap on non-economic damages (adjusted for inflation annually)

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 or three times compensatory, whichever is greater

NC.notes: North Carolina has caps on non-economic and punitive damages

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 or two times compensatory damages, whichever is greater

OH.name: Ohio

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 or three times economic damages, whichever is greater (max $350,000 for non-catastrophic injuries)

OH.notes: Ohio has complex non-economic damage cap structure

OK.name: Oklahoma

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $100,000 or actual damages, whichever is greater

OK.notes: Oklahoma Supreme Court struck down punitive cap but legislature reinstated it

OR.name: Oregon
OR.notes: Oregon has no damage caps on private defendants

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.notes: Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled damage caps unconstitutional

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.notes: Rhode Island has no damage caps

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $500,000 or three times compensatory damages, whichever is greater

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.notes: South Dakota has no damage caps

TN.name: Tennessee

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $750,000 cap on non-economic damages ($1,000,000 for catastrophic injuries)

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: $500,000 or two times compensatory damages, whichever is greater

TN.notes: Tennessee Supreme Court upheld non-economic damage caps in 2020

TX.name: Texas

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $250,000 cap on non-economic damages per defendant in medical malpractice cases

punitiveDamagesCap.rule: Two times economic damages plus non-economic damages (max $750,000) or $200,000, whichever is greater

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: $250,000 cap per defendant, $500,000 total for non-economic damages in med mal

TX.notes: Texas has caps on med mal non-economic and punitive damages

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.notes: West Virginia has no damage caps

WI.name: Wisconsin

nonEconomicDamagesCap.rule: $750,000 cap on non-economic damages for non-death medical malpractice; $500,000 for wrongful death from med mal

medicalMalpracticeCap.notes: Caps apply only to medical malpractice cases

WI.notes: Wisconsin has med mal specific caps

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.notes: Wyoming Constitution prohibits damage caps (Article 10, Section 4)

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.notes: District of Columbia has no damage caps
